bc_upper_wall.blurb: The steeper, harder half of Muscle Beach, a gymnastic sport crag in the Skaha Bluffs above Penticton in the Okanagan. All 13 routes are bolted, so bring quickdraws and little else. The wall is overhanging and broken by a big roof, and the climbing is short, powerful and bouldery, with knee-bars and pumpy sequences between angular holds. Difficulty is concentrated well into the 5.12 range, with one 5.11 and a handful of 5.13s, so this is not a place for climbers still working through moderate grades. The easier lines sit on the lower wall below.

bc_sparta_boulder_zone.blurb: A small bouldering zone in the forest near Buntzen Lake, just northeast of Vancouver, where boulders lie scattered through a talus field. The area holds 13 problems from VB to V7, and most fall in the V3 to V4 range, with a couple of easier warm-ups and a few harder lines on top. The namesake Sparta boulder sits right at the edge of the talus and climbs more cleanly than the rubble around it. Expect warm, exposed conditions on sunny days, which makes it a better choice for cooler weather. The lake and its beach are a short stroll away for a swim after the session.

bc_the_balcony_sector.blurb: A cluster of boulders on the upper talus slope of the Hunter Creek bouldering area, in the Fraser Valley near Chilliwack and Hope, with views over the river. It lies uphill of the Hillside sector and takes a moderate walk through forest on faint trails. The sector holds 13 problems from V1 to V7, and the difficulty skews hard: roughly half sit at V5 and above, with only a few easy and mid-grade options. Uneven talus landings make a couple of crash pads a good idea, and the rock is slippery in wet weather.

bc_dimension_x.blurb: A roadside cluster of boulders near the Silver Lake day-use area, in the Fraser Valley not far from Hope. The area is known for crack and offwidth problems, plus a few faces and arêtes, and many lines are on the back sides of the blocks. It has 13 problems with a wide spread, from an easy VB up to a single V12, but most sit between V1 and V3, with a couple of V7s. Roadside space beside the boulders is tight and landings can be rough in places, so check each one before you commit. A good quick stop for crack climbers.

bc_the_cooler_sector.blurb: A bouldering sector in the Oregon Jack area, southwest of Cache Creek, set in a shaded hollow among tall pines and mossy ground. It tends to feel noticeably cooler than the surrounding country. It holds 13 problems from V0 to V9. Most sit around V3, with four V0s to start on and a couple of much harder problems at the top end. A short walk on the main trail from the parking lot reaches the first boulders.

bc_icefall_brook.blurb: A remote cirque in the Rockies near Golden holding some of the biggest waterfall ice in Canada, with valley walls rising 500 metres or more. The 13 ice routes here run from WI4 to WI6, with most at WI5, so it suits strong, experienced parties. The walls face south and catch strong sun, which keeps the season short; the cirque stays cold and shaded until late winter, and trips usually target late February to early March before melting begins. Logistics are demanding and few climbers visit, so plan for a multi-day stay with a camp low in the trees.
